solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charles is after small framework for vehicle

indicators.note: the clue says the word is comes after small, fixing their order at the end

parts.note: Chas is the usual short form of the name Charles
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone called Charles follows a small frame, as if in a list of car parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The base frame of a car on which the body and engine are mounted is called this.

clue.text: Conservative runs high-class vineyard

parts.note: R stands for runs in cricket scoring
U is the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A Tory politician runs a smart wine estate.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from a 1950s British essay sorting words into U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a wine-growing estate, as in premier grand cru.

clue.text: Part of breathing apparatus to display intact, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: to air something is to display it; whole means intact, undamaged

explanation.surface: A diver's breathing kit is shown off in one piece, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells you AIR WHOLE is spoken, and its sound is spelt as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening that lets air through, such as a whale's blowhole, belongs to how a creature or device breathes.

clue.text: Blade finally opens a series of letters?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word opens

parts.note: a word is a string of letters; the question mark admits the loose definition

explanation.surface: A knife's edge ultimately reveals an inscription.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-bladed weapon is often called simply a blade in literature.

clue.text: Brother or sister returned one's flashy jewellery

indicators.note: returned means the letters of one's, written as I and S, are turned back to front

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
bling is slang for showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A family member gives back someone's gaudy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother or sister is your fellow child of the same parents, the general term for either.

clue.text: Period of not eating quickly

definitions.meaning: a spell of going without food, as in Lent or Ramadan

explanation.surface: A diet in which meals are skipped in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a stretch without food and doing something at speed.

clue.text: Jack retained by car manufacturer — it's common in Norway

indicators.note: retained by means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Ford is the American car maker
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: A man called Jack works for a car firm, and the model is popular in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Long narrow sea inlets between steep cliffs are a feature typical of the Norwegian coast.

clue.text: Telephone function Eddie resolved in half of Spalding

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit within the other piece
half of takes the first four of the eight letters of Spalding
resolved, in the sense of worked out anew, signals the letters of Eddie are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eddie fixed a phone problem while in part of a Lincolnshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the town's half around the jumbled name. Spalding is a market town in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone feature that rings a stored number at the press of one or two buttons.

clue.text: Crystalline mineral reduced, alongside old book of a certain size

indicators.note: reduced means the mineral's name loses its final letter

parts.note: quartz is a common crystalline mineral

explanation.surface: A geology volume describes a cut-down mineral next to an old book.
explanation.definitionFit: A page size made by folding a sheet twice into four leaves, and a book printed that way.

clue.text: Tiny amount shortly consumed by South African once a big drinker

indicators.note: consumed by means one piece goes inside the other as if swallowed

parts.note: a Boer was a Dutch-descended settler in South Africa, a term now historical
oz is the short form of ounce, a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A little bit is swallowed by an old Afrikaner who drinks heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a heavy drinker; in Britain it also means a pub.

clue.text: Liberal British newsman pursues fake diamond

indicators.note: pursues means the newsman comes after the rest
a fake diamond is not genuine, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword newsman

explanation.surface: A tolerant British journalist chases a counterfeit gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerant of other views and open to new ideas, the sense of liberal in attitude rather than party.

clue.text: Stock market investor and Olive perhaps prosper eventually

parts.note: a bear is a trader who expects prices to fall
the olive is an example of a fruit

explanation.surface: A trader and someone named Olive at last succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive looks like a woman's name; it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from trees yielding a crop, meaning efforts finally produce results.

clue.text: Manage awkward dame OK

indicators.note: awkward suggests something out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coping with a clumsy elderly lady is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope with whatever is available, an idiom meaning get by.

clue.text: Old-fashioned crucifix lifted in the open air

parts.note: out of fashion is out, as in flares are out

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix in a church

explanation.surface: An outdated cross is raised up out in the fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes things done outside a building, under the sky.

clue.text: French lass left in charge

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A girl from France was left running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Gaul, and so used to mean typical of France.

clue.text: Staying in bed later than usual, telling stories at home

definitions.text: Staying in bed later than usual

parts.note: telling stories means telling untruths
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone lies about being at home while sleeping late.
explanation.definitionFit: A British phrase for a lie-in, spending extra time in bed in the morning.

clue.text: Pay police on base

indicators.note: on means the police piece is placed next after the base piece

parts.note: the foot is the base of something, as of a page or mountain
the Bill is British slang for the police

explanation.surface: Pay the officers stationed at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for settling the cost, taking the charge on yourself.

clue.text: Open to view — how a pullover might be worn

definitions.text: how a pullover might be worn
definitions.meaning: a jumper goes on over a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Clearly visible: the way a jumper is worn.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into OVER T, a pullover worn over a T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Means done openly and plainly visible, the opposite of covert.

clue.text: German artist terribly stern

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: A German painter is very severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born painter of the Dada and Surrealist movements.

clue.text: Formal jacket fixed centrally during day before party

indicators.note: before puts the day piece ahead of the party
during means the central letter sits within the day

parts.note: Tue is short for Tuesday

indicators.note: centrally takes the middle letter of the word fixed

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A dinner jacket was altered in the middle of the day ahead of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for a dinner jacket, worn at formal evening events.

clue.text: Young hooligan goes round a horse, childishly worried

indicators.note: goes round means the hooligan encloses the other pieces

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A young lout circles a horse and plays on a child's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestered or fretted at; to nag is to worry someone with constant complaint.

clue.text: Important date in October added

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words October added

explanation.surface: A significant date is added to the calendar in October.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable period or point in history from which time is reckoned.

clue.text: A small bird mating

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A little bird is pairing up.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for being engaged in sex, a coy euphemism.

clue.text: Do a turn, roaming circular building

indicators.note: roaming suggests the letters wander about into a new order

explanation.surface: Wander round, doing a lap of a round building.
explanation.definitionFit: A round building or hall, usually topped by a dome.
